headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and capability conflict; default configs also create medium data-leakage and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, while Windsurf exposes workspace files and clipboard plus MCP/tool use. That creates a plausible default bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT ingests files produced by Windsurf without provenance checks
IF Windsurf copies or opens AutoGPT-generated content from the shared workspace or clipboard
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Require provenance tags on any file passed between agents
Review any tool-invoking text before execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can access files, and Windsurf explicitly reads workspace files while using broad network egress; AutoGPT also has filesystem access and allowlisted egress. If sensitive files are shared in the workspace, either agent can expose them through model or tool calls. The profiles do not prove a hard block, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace
IF either agent forwards file contents to its backend or external tools
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate least-privilege directories
Disable access to sensitive folders via ignore rules
Audit outbound requests for file-content payloads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and Windsurf can also execute shell, write files, and modify git state with shared state via local filesystem. That is a direct write-conflict pathway in default multi-instance use, with potential repository corruption or overwritten work. Uncertainty is low because both write to the same mutable surfaces.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF either agent performs git or filesystem writes without external locking
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate clone or directory
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees or branch isolation
Add a manual lock file before edits
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf’s Cascade loop can consume tool outputs and act on them, while AutoGPT produces autonomous outputs from shell/file actions. If AutoGPT’s output is treated as authoritative by Windsurf, errors can propagate into further edits or commands. The profiles show a plausible default chain, but not guaranteed irreversible harm, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses AutoGPT-generated text as input to Cascade without verification
IF either agent acts on the other’s outputs as facts or commands
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Mark inter-agent outputs as untrusted by default
Add a verification step for code or commands
Limit AutoGPT to read-only tasks when paired
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware orchestration

E_compliance.rationale: Windsurf is closed-source and runs as a user-level editor process with model-provider keys and broad egress, while AutoGPT is open-source with allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, but the mixed trust/compliance posture creates a documented-gap risk. The other agent is cited because the pair’s combined deployment is the issue.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through Windsurf’s model provider path
IF deployment policy requires only open-source or locally contained agents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Confirm vendor DPAs and retention settings
Disable optional BYOK secrets handling
Document data-flow boundaries for both agents
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance review
